subject: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)
related_links: Confluence: Template secrets and local dev policy
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

Team —

Did a final pass on the template READMEs + docs-site copy for the security/compliance section. Overall: ✅ the direction is good and we’re comfortable with the patterns as written (env-based secrets, no secrets in repo, explicit logging guidance, and “safe defaults” notes).

Before we call this “approved,” we need a few small edits + two CI checks to reduce the chance we ship foot-guns.

1) Secrets handling wording tweaks (minor, but important)
- Replace “put your key in a .env file” with “store secrets in environment variables; for local dev you may use a .env file (never commit it), and prefer your OS keychain / 1Password / Vault for anything shared.”
- Add one sentence on rotation: “If you suspect a key was exposed, revoke/rotate immediately and re-issue.” (We get this ticket a lot.)
- The existing text says “Don’t log your API key” — please broaden to “Don’t log secrets or tokens (API keys, bearer tokens, cookies, auth headers).”

2) Logging / PII guidance: clarify what we do vs what customers must do
- Current copy implies “logs are redacted.” That’s ambiguous.
- Proposed: “Templates avoid logging request/response bodies by default. If you add logging, redact PII/secrets and avoid storing raw prompts/outputs unless you have a policy + retention controls.”
- Also: specify that correlation IDs are safe to log (request_id/trace_id), but “tenant identifiers should be stable IDs, not emails.”

3) CI checks (must-have for launch)
- Secret scanning: enable gitleaks (or equivalent) on the quickstarts repo, including blocking patterns for common key formats.
- Guardrail check: a simple CI grep/lint that fails if any template includes “Authorization:” or “REDWOOD_API_KEY=” in committed example outputs/log snippets.

I attached a doc with suggested wording edits. If you want, we can add a small “Security checklist” box in each template README with 5 bullets (no secrets in repo, no prompt/output logging by default, allow-list tools, timeouts/retries, dependency updates).

Let me know who should implement the CI checks (I assume Sahana/Connor, but happy to route).

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance (Product)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: quickstart-security-guidance-edits-2026-02-03.docx
Attachment: gitleaks-config-redwood-quickstarts.toml


From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

Thanks Naomi.

This is all reasonable. Wei + I can land the docs wording edits today.

Two questions:
1) For “prefer OS keychain / 1Password / Vault” — OK to keep that as “examples” and not a requirement? (We don’t want to imply we provide those.)
2) For the CI grep/lint, are we aiming to catch *any* “Authorization” string, or only in example logs? I worry we may get false positives from HTTP client code.

Also +1 on a short Security checklist callout box; I can add it consistently across all three templates.

— Elliot


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:26 AM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

On (1) yes — examples only. Suggest language:
“Use environment variables for secrets. For local development, you may load them from a .env file (never commit it). For shared/dev/staging environments, use your organization’s secret manager (e.g., 1Password, Vault, AWS/GCP/Azure secret managers).”

On (2) we should scope the grep so we’re not chasing false positives. Options:
- Only scan docs/README + example output blocks.
- Or scan any committed files under templates/**/README* and docs/** for “Authorization:” and common key formats.

The goal is to catch “copy/paste this curl command with a real key” and “print headers on error” patterns.


From: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 12:18 PM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

We can implement the docs edits by EOD.

Plan:
- Update the secrets section in each template README to match Marcus’s suggested language.
- Update the “Observability / logging” section to remove “logs are redacted” and replace with “templates avoid logging bodies by default; redact if you add it; avoid logging raw prompts/outputs.”
- Add a one-line note in each template about correlation IDs: “Log request_id/trace_id; use stable tenant IDs (not emails).”

For CI: looping in Connor/Sahana separately, but do we have a preferred secret scanning baseline? (gitleaks seems easiest).


From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 1:07 PM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

+1 gitleaks.

Two small adds from audit/SIEM perspective (wording only):
- Where we mention “telemetry,” explicitly say “do not include personal data in telemetry attributes.” We should keep the telemetry contract high-signal/low-risk.
- Add a retention caveat: “If you enable prompt/output logging, consider retention and access controls.” (This comes up in customer security reviews.)

Doesn’t need to be long — one sentence each.


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Quickstart templates — security review: secrets handling + logging guidance (final pass)

All sounds good.

Answers / final asks:
- Secret manager examples: yes, keep as examples (not Redwood-provided).
- CI grep: scope to docs + README + “examples output” snippets only. The goal is preventing us from publishing headers/keys in docs, not analyzing runtime code.
- Secret scanning: gitleaks baseline is approved. Use the attached config as a starting point; OK to tune to reduce noise.

Please incorporate Kevin’s two SIEM/audit sentences (no personal data in telemetry attributes; retention/access controls if you enable prompt/output logging).

Once the docs edits are in and CI checks are added (ENG-2849), Security can mark the template guidance section as approved for launch.

— Naomi
